concepts.title: overview
concepts.source: Make concept materialization **lazy** so `create` stops decomposing every plan into a full concept tree up front, and instead surfaces — for operator confirmation — only the concepts the tool proposes to **defer** or mark **won't-do**. This is the MVP of the original desire ("confirm the list of deferred concepts"): materialize a concept record entry only at a deferral decision, surface those (and only those) for confirmation, and leave un-deferred plans with no concept record at all. The shipped hierarchical machinery (the tree, `Step.concept_ids`, `synchronize_concepts`) stays in place but dormant-by-default — this does not rip it out. Expected decomposition ~5–7 steps; if convergence pressure grows it past that, defer to the backlog (BACKLOG #129) rather than growing the plan.

concepts.title: problem statement
concepts.source: Today `create` **eagerly** builds a concept tree for every plan whether or not anything is deferred. `bootstrap_concepts` (`plan_tool/concept_bootstrap.py:55`, called unconditionally at `plan_tool/create.py:5932`) emits one node per body section (~8), and `emit_concept_tree` (`plan_tool/concept_tree.py:330`, invoked at `plan_tool/create.py:5956` when no saved tree exists) enriches that to ~20 more speculative sub-concepts — 28 nodes in the shipped `concept-write-integrity` example, all `review_state="unreviewed"`, `decision="include"`. Almost none are ever deferred; they are the plan's prose re-encoded as a second structure that must be kept in sync — the coupling that produced the write-integrity bugs and the whole-bundle-fingerprint staleness that broke that plan's audit twice during authoring. Three specific problems, grounded: (1) **Eager over-decomposition** — `emit_concept_tree` at `create.py:5956` adds ~20 speculative sub-concepts nobody signs off on; that enrichment is the bloat, the sync surface, and (via the whole-bundle `compute_plan_fingerprint` on `load_concepts`, `plan_tool/concept_tree.py:234`) the staleness coupling, so any plan/detail edit invalidates the record even when no deferral decision changed. (2) **The confirm gate reviews the wrong thing and is silent under `-y`** — `_review_create_concepts` (`plan_tool/create.py:4506-4537`) walks the whole tree (include/defer/wont_do per node) and is skipped non-interactively (`create.py:4516-4517`), silently accepting the tool's suggestions — the exact founding-incident failure (BACKLOG #121), since these plans are authored with `-y`. (3) **The deferral producers already exist but don't gate** — the three defer points (create-synthesis, already record-driven and told to abstain at `prompts/synthesize-body.md:88-94`; the decomposition "a branch with no namable live scenario is NOT a step — defer it" instruction at `create.py:1983-1984`, which silently omits from the step array; and detail's shared-find routing, `detail.py:399-427`, bounded to a pre-approved `decision="defer"` node by `detail.py:1683-1691`) none stop to confirm a *new* deferral.

concepts.title: architecture
concepts.source: Keep the shipped record format and its writer; change *when and how much* gets materialized. Most of the lazy behavior is already latent: `scope-review` (`plan_tool/cli/scope_review_cmd.py:41-119`) already re-derives the tree from live plan text every run and tolerates an absent record (`original_tree is None` → bootstrap directly, `scope_review_cmd.py:57-64`), making it the natural materialize+sign-off hook; and the coverage findings (`check_concept_coverage`, `plan_tool/review.py:2290-2380`) are already inert on an absent/`None`/all-unreviewed tree (`review.py:2312, 2317`), firing only on `review_state=="approved"` nodes — so an empty-until-deferred record produces zero findings until an operator signs off. Five changes: **A. Stop eager enrichment** — do not call `emit_concept_tree` at create; the record is either absent (preferred for the common case) or a thin section-only bootstrap, deciding during detailing which is cleaner given the `create`-writes-a-tree test coupling (`create.py:5932-5974`; tests assert `concepts.json` exists post-create — the main breakage surface). Enrichment becomes dead code for the create path; leave the function for possible reuse but stop invoking it eagerly. **B. Deferral-focused confirmation** — replace the whole-tree walk with a gate that surfaces only proposed `defer` / `wont_do` decisions; an included concept needs no confirmation and no record (a committed step is its own proof; coverage is already inert on unreviewed). **C. Safe under `-y`** (closes the founding incident) — non-interactively, a proposed deferral is recorded **unconfirmed**, never silently accepted; make an unconfirmed proposed deferral a blocking signal so it cannot ship unseen. The `concept-unsigned-deferral` source exists (`review.py:2235`, today info-only); this plan's decision is whether to promote a proposed-but-unconfirmed defer to blocking or surface it in the run summary + `list --status`. The operator confirms later via `scope-review` (already lazy). **D. Materialize at the defer points, via the existing hook** — at each defer decision (B/C above, and detail's shared-find routing), materialize the one concept + its proposed decision through `scope-review`'s derive+sign-off path, which already runs on an absent tree. Preserve detail's precondition that a deferral references a signed-off `decision="defer"` node (`detail.py:1683-1691`) — lazy means "materialize+sign off as part of the defer action," not "reference nothing." **E. Record stays small and decision-keyed** — only defer/wont_do decisions and their confirmation state; this breaks the whole-bundle-fingerprint staleness coupling for the common case, since an un-deferred plan has no record and thus no fingerprint to go stale.

concepts.title: out of scope
concepts.source:
- Removing the hierarchical tree, `parent_path`/`depth`, or `Step.concept_ids` — leave the shipped machinery in place but dormant; migration/deletion is a separate decision. `split` / `merge` / `reground` / `scope-out` conservation of `concept_ids` keeps working on whatever ids exist (empty is the valid default).
- The `concept-write-integrity` transactional hardening and BACKLOG #126–#128 — largely moot for the lazy path (fewer/smaller writers, no big record to diverge from prose); this seed supersedes that path for the common flow rather than completing it.
- New schema, commands, or a rewrite of `concept_sync` — reuse `scope-review`'s derive+sign-off.

concepts.title: risks
concepts.source:
- The `create`-writes-a-tree test coupling is the main breakage surface (change A); budget a step to reconcile those tests to "absent record is valid."
- Promoting unconfirmed deferrals to blocking (change C) could block legitimate `-y` batch authoring; gate the decision behind evidence and offer a surface-not-block fallback.

concepts.title: testing
concepts.source:
- **Un-deferred plan:** `create -y` produces no blocking findings and (per A's decision) either no `concepts.json` or a thin section-only one; no `emit_concept_tree` call.
- **Founding-incident regression:** a `create -y` whose decomposition proposes a deferral leaves an **unconfirmed** deferral that the completeness/run summary surfaces (or blocks on), never a silently-accepted one.
- **Lazy materialization:** a `scope-review` defer on a plan with no prior record creates exactly the one deferred concept, signed off, and renders it into `## Deferred` (reuses the existing `render_scope_decisions` path).
- **Staleness:** editing an un-deferred plan's prose does not raise `StaleConceptTreeError` anywhere (there is no record to invalidate).

concepts.title: deferred
concepts.source:
- Whether to keep a thin section bootstrap or go fully record-absent at create (change A) — decide from the test-coupling cost during detailing.
- Enforcing a seed-declared step ceiling and the program-scale monitoring that would have caught the original blowup — BACKLOG #129.
